stories.title: World Series Game 2 Recap — Brewers 5, Rays 4. Milwaukee Leads 2-0
stories.angle: Milwaukee was down 4-0 in the second inning and still won. The Brewers' bullpen entered with the game already a mess after Henderson's rocky start — and delivered 6 scoreless innings. Sal Frelick's HR tied it at 4-4. Cooper Pratt's go-ahead RBI single in the 7th put Milwaukee ahead. Aaron Ashby struck out Yandy Díaz for the save in the 9th. Brewers now lead the World Series 2-0.

stories.title: World Series Game 3 Preview — Peralta Faces Former Team at Tropicana Field
stories.angle: Monday's Game 3 brings the World Series to Tropicana Field for the first time since 2008 — and the storyline writes itself. Freddy Peralta (ALCS MVP, 2-0, 0.75 ERA) starts for Tampa Bay against Milwaukee, the franchise where he spent eight seasons. He was traded to the Mets in January 2026, then acquired by Tampa Bay at the deadline. Robert Gasser (1.00 ERA postseason) starts for the Brewers. Game 3 is Monday October 26 at 8 PM ET on FOX.

stories.title: Brewers Bullpen — 1.33 ERA, 40+ Postseason Innings, and the Engine of a Comeback
stories.angle: The Brewers bullpen is the best story in this World Series. In Game 2, they entered with the Brewers already down 4-0 — Henderson had given up a crooked first inning — and delivered 6 scoreless innings from Romero through Ashby. Their postseason ERA across the NLCS and World Series now stands at 1.33 over 40⅔ innings. It is the single biggest reason Milwaukee is two wins from their first championship.

stories.title: Frelick and Pratt — The Unlikely Heroes of Game 2
stories.angle: When the Brewers were down 4-0, nobody was calling on Sal Frelick or Cooper Pratt to save the series. Frelick's home run tied the game at 4-4. Pratt's RBI single in the 7th put Milwaukee ahead for good. Two role players stepping up in the biggest game of their careers is the kind of storyline that defines World Series runs.

stories.title: Rays Down 2-0 — Is There a Path Back?
stories.angle: Teams down 2-0 in the World Series win about 21% of the time historically. But the Rays have Freddy Peralta (ALCS MVP) going tomorrow at home and Drew Rasmussen (1.29 ERA in the postseason) still available. Junior Caminero at 22 — 45 HR and 110 RBI in 2025, 13 HR this October run — is a legitimate offensive weapon. Games 3-5 are at Tropicana Field, where the Rays went 3-1 in the postseason. The series is not over.

x_posts.text:
